correctness.rationale: For symmetric C, orthogonal spectral decomposition reduces the toral map to determinant-one 2x2 matrices with positive log multipliers Phi(d)=2 asinh(|d|/2). If n is a multiple of three, the graph is exactly complete tripartite and has spectrum 2m,-m,-m,0. In the other two residue classes, two polynomial identities over Z[z] yield every Fourier eigenvalue; n not divisible by three prevents denominators zero on sampled nth roots of unity. The symbol poles have only logarithmic entropy singularities; a discrete distance lower bound and controlled log-sum prove uniform integrability and Riemann-sum convergence to positive finite constants. All hypotheses/normalizations and neutral modes are explicit. The included script independently checks arithmetic/frequencies but is not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The natural stride-three graph family was explicitly proposed to study how connectivity affects chaotic entropy. The result finds a nontrivial arithmetic boundary: neighboring networks have exactly the same vertex degree and similar density, but one congruence class collapses to rank-three coupling and has logarithmic total entropy, while two other classes have positive entropy per site. This is a structural nonuniform thermodynamic limit, not an arbitrary example or a small numerical improvement; exact symbols and constants make the qualitative paradox quantitatively reproducible.
